title: ReLoop: Structured Modeling and Behavioral Verification for Reliable LLM-Based Optimization
claim: A generate-verify-repair loop catches silent errors by testing solver behavior and feeding diagnosed failures back into regeneration.
layout: Nested stacked panels, top-down flow, dashed feedback loops, traffic-light verdict branches
description: A flowchart of the full system. At top left, a pink box holds the inputs, a problem text document and a data table. Arrows lead into a lavender Structured Generation panel. It chains Understanding, Math Spec and Code, and a dashed sub-box expands Math Spec into Sets, Params, Vars, Constraints and Objective. A downward arrow enters a light-blue Behavioral Verification panel. This panel has a Solver block and a darker Verification block with L1 (execution, duality) and L2 (behavioral testing) steps. Three outcomes branch below: green PASS, yellow WARNING and red FATAL. PASS leads to verified output. WARNING leads to targeted repair, then a safety and regression diamond, then rollback or output with warnings. Dashed lines loop back to the solver and to code regeneration. Small icons mark each block. Pastel fills and the traffic-light colors guide the eye.
caption: ReLoop overview. Structured Generation follows expert modeling practice: understand the problem, formalize the mathematical model with explicit variable-type reasoning, synthesize Gurobi code with data extraction, and self-verify completeness. Behavioral Verification: L1 checks execution correctness (FATAL blocks output); L2 tests constraint (CPT) and objective (OPT) presence via solver-based perturbation (WARNING/PASS). Diagnosis-Guided Repair: FATAL triggers diagnosis-specific regeneration (syntax tracebacks, IIS, or unbounded rays); WARNING triggers targeted repair with regression rollback. When the budget N is exhausted, ReLoop returns the best verified code.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can translate natural-language problem descriptions into optimization code, but the code is prone to silent failures: it executes and returns a solver-feasible solution while encoding a semantically incorrect formulation. On compositional problems, the resulting feasibility-correctness gap reaches 90 percentage points. We introduce ReLoop, which combines two mechanisms. Structured generation decomposes code production into a four-stage reasoning chain (understand, formalize, synthesize, verify) to reduce formulation errors during generation. Behavioral verification detects the errors that remain by testing whether the formulation responds correctly to solver-based parameter perturbation, a signal that comes from the solver rather than from LLM self-review and requires no ground truth. The two mechanisms address different error structures: structured generation gives the largest gain on compositional problems (+8.5pp accuracy on RetailOpt-190 with Claude Opus 4.6), and behavioral verification gives its largest gain on localized defects (+4.4pp on MAMO-ComplexLP). With diagnostic execution recovery, ReLoop reaches 100% executable code on Claude Opus 4.6, and relative to direct generation it raises or preserves every reported metric of the three chat-tuned foundation models on all three benchmarks. For the narrowly fine-tuned SFT model we test, the chain-of-thought prompt conflicts with its learned output format and lowers its accuracy on MAMO-ComplexLP; we document and analyze this interaction. We release RetailOpt-190, 190 compositional retail optimization scenarios in which several constraints interact.
